gen-gf-gugi-gf-holtwood-one-sc: Holtwood One SC reads wide-tracked and towering, its curves closing to slivers. Gugi comes in after it with one flat line weight and open letters, so a longer stretch of the body feels dense and ceremonial.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-manuale: Gugi looks like sign-shop vinyl cut to a single line width, tall and bold. Manuale follows with large-eyed lowercase and moderate contrast, so a longer stretch of it reads traditional and settled.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-naskh-arabic: Noto Naskh Arabic reads like lightly engraved brass, with a very tall x-height and a modest contrast. And Gugi, with curves as hefty as a rope's body, handles the shouting while the text serif handles the fine, etched detail.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-nastaliq-urdu: Gugi has a pipe-cleaner feel in every letterform, tall and boldly open. Noto Nastaliq Urdu handles the quieter work, tracing ink with a soft, restrained thick-thin ratio and tight vertical rhythm.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-rashi-hebrew: Gugi's neatly bent pipe-cleaner texture, with tall lowercase and open terminals, is what you notice first. Noto Rashi Hebrew supplies the quality that holds it together: a lightly engraved, bookish restraint beside all that bold.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-ahom: Noto Serif Ahom reads lofty and dignified, with joins that taper modestly without vanishing. Gugi lays fine rope strokes above it, and over a longer stretch the text serif keeps its slight but clear modulation.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-armenian: Traditional in its bearing, Noto Serif Armenian has big open counters and mild contrast, while Gugi draws everything in pencil-line consistency. One is bold and tall; the other is gentle.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-balinese: Noto Serif Balinese reads with great vertical presence and a calm ebb and flow of stroke thickness. Gugi brings bent-tubing lines on top, and that mix of rope-like boldness and classic serif ease is the pair's draw.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-bengali: Ribbon-cut and confident, Gugi holds one constant width and open terminals throughout. But Noto Serif Bengali does the reading work, with slightly thinner hairlines and soft accents of heavier strokes.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-devanagari: Round, tall, and unmistakably bold: that is Gugi, whose o is a ring with a constant wall. Noto Serif Devanagari sits beneath with medium contrast and short ascenders, softening that rigid heading into something bookish.
